restrictions.statement: Import only the Python standard library (its own compiled modules included) and Python source files under `/app`, load no other native code (through `ctypes`, for example), and do not start other programs
restrictions.how: every graded run goes through tests/guard.py, which ends the run on a process start, on native code (ctypes, or an extension module from outside the standard library), and on an import from outside the standard library and the delivered files, counting an installed package under the standard-library directory as outside it. Since revision-v6 the rules live only in the closure of the audit hook, built from interpreter functions captured before the program starts, so rebinding names in the launcher's module, os, posix or builtins changes nothing (v6 finding 28); the launcher replaces _posixsubprocess.fork_exec, which raises no audit event, stops a fresh import of that helper and stops gc.get_objects/get_referrers/get_referents. Nine probe programs, one per route, and one ordinary program check it. Revision-v7 states that the standard library's own compiled modules (math, _decimal, …) are allowed, which the guard always permitted; plain.py imports math to show it. Revision-v8 (v8 findings 3 and 14): the rule now allows any Python source file delivered under /app, which is exactly what the guard checks (it cannot tell a vendored pure-Python module from one the candidate wrote), and the guard no longer refuses an /app path merely for holding a site-packages component; it also stops sqlite3.enable_load_extension and sqlite3.load_extension, and a tenth probe, sqlite_ext.py, checks that route.
